question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $14,$ the additive inverse of $-10$ modulo $14$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $-10$ modulo $14$ is the integer $0\le x<14$ such that

$$
x+(-10)≡0\,(\text{mod}\,14).
$$

Notice that $10+(-10)≡0,$ so $x≡10\,(\text{mod}\,14),$ which is already in the required form. 

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $-10$ modulo $14$ is $10.$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
